segmentation.text: Any pedestrian who is not wholly or partially blind
or any driver of any vehicle
who approaches or comes in contact with
a person wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person
and take such precautions before proceeding
as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). 'who is not wholly or partially blind' leaves out the pedestrians the law protects; blindness itself is no observable, and is read through the feature the same sentence names as its sign: the subject is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal ('pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'), which carries no exclusion of its own.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions of devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and electric scooters, which the reading classifies). 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is the role of who controls the vehicle, never membership: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same atoms as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

'comes in contact with' is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', taken at the observation at which it begins; a near miss is not contact, its exclusion, and is read by 'approaches'. 'approaches' is the subject, while not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt), coming within a reach of the person: the centre-to-centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') falls to p.blind_person_approach_reach. That atom is not read as a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival, its exclusions: only as how near the subject has come.

The person protected is identified by the features the words list: 'carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person' is ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, 'pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'. 'a person wholly or partially blind' with those features is the pedestrian the class describes: the ontology's class for exactly this description, whose contract states no exclusion. The person is another road user than the subject, quantified in the applicability.

'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies by its own scope ('when required, means complete cessation from movement'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 is scoped to stopping 'when prohibited'). 'come to a full stop' is drv.motion.complete_halt, whose contract quotes that definition: 'The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement'.

operationalizations.convention: The stop is immediate when the subject is at rest within a window ahead of the approach or contact event no longer than a perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed (AASHTO stopping-sight-distance model).

residues.why: 'with wisdom' qualifies the person assisting, not the person protected; that the person assisted is wholly or partially blind and is being assisted is what identifies the protected person, and a helper's wisdom, a state of mind no trace shows, does not change that identification, so the duty owed to the person assisted is the same whether or not the helper's wisdom holds.

applicability: The subject is either a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, or a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) read through its controlled motion; and at the judged observation, for some other road user b of the scene (not the same as the subject) of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, an approach or contact event occurs: rel.contact between the subject and b holds here and did not at the previous observation, or rel.centre_distance between them is at most p.blind_person_approach_reach here and was not at the previous observation while the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance).
obligation: At each observation at which such an event occurs, the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the window ahead of length p.immediate_stop_window, measured in time on the subject. No halt in that window is violated; a window that reaches past the end of the trace without a halt is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motor vehicle (ru.motor_vehicle) moving at 10 m/s comes within p.blind_person_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance) of a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal at the kerb and keeps moving: no observation of the window p.immediate_stop_window ahead has kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same vehicle decelerates and is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) within p.immediate_stop_window after the centre distance first falls to the reach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle drives past an ordinary pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane, not led); no road user of class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal stands near the vehicle's path; rel.centre_distance is not observed and no contact occurs, so whether the vehicle approached is unknown; the vehicle does not halt.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject is itself a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal walking toward another such pedestrian.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane) walking comes into rel.contact with a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal and keeps walking, never at rest within p.immediate_stop_window.

param_proposals.name: p.blind_person_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the centre distance within which a moving road user has approached a pedestrian carrying a white cane or led by another person: the stopping distance from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s with a 1 s perception-reaction time and a 4.5 m/s^2 deceleration
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_stop_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest time from the moment a stop is due until the road user is at rest for the stop to be immediate: a 1 s perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s at 4.5 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph
